title: Reject slice examples that name a removed flag
lead: S107's acceptance text still said `--require-render` after that flag had been renamed to `--strict`.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** rewriting old done slices, or checking `docs/agents.md`.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Nothing in `slicer check` reads the `slicer …` commands written inside a slice. A removed flag can sit in Failing tests until an agent copies it into the skill, where the parser then rejects it. S105 renamed `--require-render` to `--strict`, and the S107 slice filed afterward still spelled the old flag.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` or the check path that already walks slice text
- `tests/` for the new check
- `docs/agents.md` only if the check's problem shape needs a line

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. An open slice whose section body contains a backtick command `slicer next --require-render` makes `slicer check` fail. The problem names the slice id, the section heading, and the unknown flag.
2. A backtick command the parser accepts, including `--render --strict`, is not a problem.
3. Done and retired slices are not scanned, so history can keep the old flag name.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: When checking an open slice, collect backtick spans that start with `slicer `, parse each with the real parser, and report unknown flags. Do not try to execute the command or require the id to exist. Leave prose that merely mentions a flag outside backticks alone.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The three cases above pass. `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` and `slicer check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit. Do not tag or push.
